governance.attested_by: miso16 st-gas-intermediate 2026-06-27 (KEEPER on faithfulness grounds, supersedes miso15 ct-intermediate)
governance.note: MISO's legacy gas-steam (ST_GAS) fleet runs INTERMEDIATE-duty, not as peakers, but inherited ERCOT-fitted steam parameters that under-ran it (the Moselle / Lewis Creek under-run) and let it stop-start with peaker agility. EIA-860 confirms the named units are genuine NG steam (prime mover ST): Harding Street 990, Ames Electric 1122, Nine Mile Point 1403, Lewis Creek 3457 (Entergy Texas, MISO South), Sabine 3459 (Entergy Texas), plus Little Gypsy 1402, Big Cajun 1 1464, Brame 6190, Moselle 2070 ST unit. ONE consolidated config-gated lever (--st-gas-intermediate, default OFF so miso15 and every other ISO reproduce byte-identical) bundles THREE well-grounded corrections, each tracing to a measured/physical input and assigning an offer SHAPE or a physical availability, never pinning measured output: (1) OFFER CURVE -- route the measured CAMPD median-CF>=50 cohort (fleet.st_gas_intermediate_plants, derived from thermal_tranches_MISO.csv median_cf: 990=61.8, 1122=67.4, 1403=63.5, 3457=67.0, 3459=60.2, 1891=59.2 -- a forward-reproducible duty-role signal, same admissibility class as ct_intermediate_plants / ST_GAS_PEAKER_PLANTS) to a flatter ST_GAS_INTERMEDIATE curve (committed 0.85 / econ 1.00-1.15 / peak 2.20 / 6% peaking) so its sustained energy clears at intermediate load instead of being priced above the CC fleet by the steep ERCOT peaker-shaped ST_GAS curve (econ_high 1.40, peak 4.20, 15% peaking); (2) STARTUP COST -- feed the gas-steam startup cost + min-run (constants.ST_GAS_COMMITMENT_PARAMS: 55-75 $/MW, 12-24 h min-run, from NREL/SR-5500-55433 + OEM specs) into the P1 season-spread bid markup so a stop-start costs more than idling and the steam fleet DRAGS rather than cycling like a peaker; (3) DERATE -- replace the ERCOT-fitted ST_GAS WEFOR base (THERMAL_AVAILABILITY 0.21, >2x every other thermal class, an implicit availability crush atop the EIA-860 net-summer rating) with a realistic NERC-GADS gas-steam EFOR (0.10), keeping the age escalation. RESULT vs the miso15 baseline (re-solved 2024, identical command minus --st-gas-intermediate): ST_GAS 2024 12.93 -> 15.89 TWh (+2.96, the targeted under-run lift), with CC_REGULAR essentially UNCHANGED (164.80 -> 164.58) -- the gain is attributable to steam, not displaced CC; gas total 234.22 -> 236.43 TWh (toward EIA-923 257.84); 2024 energy-balance drift +0.92 TWh (INSIDE +/-3.0 tol, vs miso15 -0.39); 2023 gas 218.3 -> 221.0 (toward 249) with net import 39.0 -> 37.6 TWh (actual 37.9, CLOSER). Determination NOT-YET (the broader MISO gas under-run and the high-gas-2025 coal over-run / seam export remain -- see model_miss_notes), but strictly more structurally faithful than miso15 on the targeted ST_GAS dimension. No unit pinned to its observed CEMS generation; no input rescaled so the model output lands on actuals; the median-CF cohort assigns an offer SHAPE only and the WEFOR/startup values are a priori physical constants, not fits to the price/volume residual.

model_miss_notes: Exceptions ledger EMPTY by design: every out-of-tolerance criterion is a genuine MODEL MISS for a later lever, not an accepted measured-input limitation. The isolated misses and their next levers: (1) BROADER GAS UNDER-RUN persists (2023 gas 221.0 vs EIA-923 248.98; 2024 236.4 vs 257.84): the +2.96 ST_GAS lift is real but the bulk of the gas gap is the CC fleet and the import under-model, NOT the steam fleet -- a separate lever (CC offer curve / seam import deliverability). (2) 2025 ENERGY-BALANCE OVER-RUN +23.41 TWh is COAL-driven, not steam: in the high-gas 2025 year (Henry Hub $3.52) the model runs coal hard (231.6 vs EIA-923 201.0, +30.6) and exports the surplus (model net -18.0 vs actual +19.0 TWh import) because the priced seam node lets cheap coal out -- a pre-existing MISO coal-take-or-pay / seam-deliverability miss unchanged by the steam levers (drag-off this run is +23.41 vs the discarded drag-on probe's +30.08, i.e. the steam change did not cause it). Next lever: MISO coal high-gas-year offer curve + seam export cap. (3) WEATHER-DEPENDENT MUST-RUN FLOOR (Little Gypsy / River load-pocket) DEFERRED: the net-load reliability-drag floor was deliberately NOT enabled -- its ScenarioConfig coefficients (slope 0.00906, cap 0.34) are ERCOT-derived and SATURATE at the 0.34 cap across all of MISO's larger net-load range (60-110 GW), degenerating into a flat 34% must-run that force-ran ~14 TWh of steam and suppressed imports (the discarded drag-on probe drove 2023 import below actual and 2025 to +30 TWh). It needs a MISO-specific regression (MISO overnight ST_GAS CAMPD CF vs MISO net-load), mirroring the per-ISO ERCOT/NYISO/CAISO floor derivations, before it can be a keeper lever; the wiring is in place (--gas-st-netload-drag) awaiting MISO coefficients. (4) PARTIAL-PLANT IN-WINDOW RETIREMENTS (Dan E Karn coal 1A/1B/2A/2B, 544 MW SUB, retired May-2023 while the gas units 3/4 stay operable; similarly A B Brown, South Oak Creek, Waterford 1&2) are NOT modeled running their pre-retirement months: the COD ramp is plant-keyed (one retirement date per plant), so process_eia860.build_within_window_retirees emits whole-plant exits only. Whole-plant MISO in-window retirees (Baxter Wilson 2050, Carl Bailey 202, Lansing 1047, etc.) ARE captured. Generator-keyed COD is the fix; modest 2023 effect for one partially-retired plant.
